basics.body: Ten units that follow real surahs, from الناس back to الضحى, then الفاتحة and beyond. Lessons open one after another; each unit ends with a finale passage you recite, which opens the next unit.
Seven short steps: hear real words, notice the sound, learn the rule, say it, find it in an ayah, check yourself, then recite a passage. At most two new lessons a day.
Every rule you learn is asked daily for a week, then after 3, 7, 14, 30, 60 and 120 days. Answer right and it waits longer; answer wrong and it comes back sooner.
The app never grades your recitation. If you have a teacher, plan what to recite, log corrections in class, and they come back in your review until fixed.

blocks.text: Ten units (0–9) that follow the surahs of the intro course by المهندس علاء حامد: الناس back towards الضحى, then الفاتحة, then rules from beyond جزء عمّ, then المخارج والصفات in full.

items.text: Lessons open one after another. Today always shows the next one.
At most two new lessons a day. Spacing is what makes them stick.
After a unit's last lesson comes its finale: a passage you recite. “I recited it” opens the next unit.
Some units list lines of تحفة الأطفال or الجزرية to memorise. They are optional.
اسمع Hear: three real words with the rule, from the reciter. Play each as often as you like.
لاحظ Notice: two words, one with the sound you just heard and one without. Which is which, by ear? Then both are named.
تعلّم Learn: the rule card, with its name, definition and examples.
ردّد Say: repeat after the reciter, record yourself, compare, and say if it sounded the same.
استخرج Find: tap every word in an ayah that has the rule.
تحقّق Check: two or three quick questions.
اقرأ Recite: a real passage that uses only rules you know. Listen, recite, record, then “I recited it”.

blocks.text: Leave mid-lesson and it resumes at the same step the same day. Finished lessons can be replayed from the course map.

items.text: سبق: today's new lesson.
سبقي: lessons of the past week. Each is asked every day for its first week.
منزل: older lessons. They return after 3, 7, 14, 30, 60, then 120 days. A wrong answer brings the rule back the next day and starts its ladder again.

blocks.tail: . Strong means a month of right answers on different examples.

blocks.text: If more than 15 reviews are overdue, new lessons pause until you catch up. The practice card on Today lists your recent passages to recite again.

items.text: Before class: Teacher tab → Plan a session. The app suggests your unit finale and corrections to re-check.
In class: tap the word your teacher corrected, choose the rule and whether it was clear (جلي) or subtle (خفي).
After class: mark the finale passed or not yet (passed opens the next unit). Corrections join your review.
Next class: re-check each correction. “Fixed” closes it; “still wrong” sends its rule back to the start.
Rules tab: every rule card, the mind map, and confusing pairs. Open any card any time, even before its lesson.
Colours in the Quran text are the tajweed colours of the printed coloured muṣḥaf. Turn them off in the player with “Colours off”.
The player can loop, slow down, and pause after each ayah for you to repeat.
Cards marked “needs teacher” have a point the sources disagree on. Ask your teacher.
Your progress is kept on this device by default. No account is needed.
If you sign in (optional), your progress is backed up to our server and kept in step on your other devices.
Your recordings never leave this device, signed in or not.
Not signed in? Install the app to your home screen so the browser doesn't clear it, and save a backup file from Settings now and then.
Sign in from Settings with an email link or Google to back up and sync your progress.
Teacher link: a read-only page of your progress for your teacher. You can turn it off any time.
A circle (حلقة) is a small group of friends who see who studied on which days this week. No scores and no ranking.
